creative_brief.emotional_promise: Open a tiny moon gate, aim one familiar light, and discover three crisp creatures with one obvious hand motion.
creative_brief.format_rationale: Four compact pages separate recognition and one-time assembly from optical setup, first play, reset, troubleshooting, and safety, leaving enough room for exact product visuals and readable owner-facing instructions.
creative_brief.physical_format: Four-page A5 portrait booklet (148 × 210 mm), designed as a folded in-box leaflet.
teaching_arc: Recognize all four loose parts before assembly.
Assemble the captured reel and kickstand once.
Orient the PHONE and WALL sides correctly.
Place phone, gate, and wall at the supported distances.
Align rabbit home, then turn to fox and owl.
Reset, troubleshoot, and pack away safely.
typography: Embedded Bitstream Vera Bold for display, navigation, labels, and numbered actions.
Embedded Bitstream Vera for instructions, captions, limitations, and safety guidance.
creative_brief.visual_motif: Moon portals, a widening beam, indexed arc marks, and exact cast silhouettes make every page feel like a miniature proscenium rather than a technical report.

findings: The first complete render clipped the sentence explaining indexed stops and the intentional eclipse wipe at the right trim on page 3.
The first complete render showed a missing-glyph box in the page-4 arrow-to-double-V reset pill.
The first complete render named the four parts but did not visually inventory each loose part, and its assembly sequence relied on unexplained mechanical jargon.
Several instruction blocks in the first complete render were undersized for an in-box manual, and its footer sat too close to the trim edge.
resolved_changes: Wrapped and enlarged the indexed-stop explanation so the full eclipse-wipe sentence remains inside the page-3 text area.
Replaced the unsupported arrow glyph with the explicit text 'ARROW POINTS TO DOUBLE-V' and clarified the reset stopping action.
Added exact-derived thumbnails for all four loose parts plus a four-frame assembly sequence with outward-facing peg, layer-order, latch-corner, and do-not-force cues.
Enlarged owner-facing body text where space allowed and moved every footer line and page number inward to a safer print margin.

Bound embedded rasters to print-appropriate 180 dpi to satisfy the decoded-stream limit without changing their sealed visual sources, then re-rendered and directly inspected all four changed pages in color and grayscale; identity, sequence, distance, reset, troubleshooting, and safety cues remained legible without color dependence.
